lessons.title: The mole and number of particles
lessons.description: Connect amount of substance in moles with the number of particles.
lessons.content: The mole is a counting unit for a very large number of particles. One mole contains approximately 6.02 × 10²³ specified particles. The relationship is number of particles = amount in moles × Avogadro constant.
learning_objectives: Explain why chemists use the mole as a counting unit.
Calculate particle number from amount in moles.
prerequisites: Use standard form and multiply simple numbers.

explanation_sections.title: Counting chemical particles
explanation_sections.body: Atoms and molecules are too small to count one at a time in laboratory samples. The mole groups particles into a fixed count. State whether the particles are atoms, molecules, ions or another specified entity.

explanation_sections.title: Using the relationship
explanation_sections.body: N = n × Nₐ, where N is particle number, n is amount in moles and Nₐ ≈ 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹. Recap: multiply moles by the Avogadro constant; keep track of what particles are being counted.

worked_examples.prompt: How many molecules are in 2 mol of a molecular substance?

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: Approximately how many particles are in 1 mol?
questions.explanation: One mole contains approximately Avogadro's number of specified particles.

questions.prompt: How many atoms are in 0.5 mol of atoms? Use Nₐ = 6.02 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.
In the relationship N = nNₐ, what does n represent?
questions.explanation: The symbol n represents amount of substance, measured in moles.

lessons.title: Molar mass and amount of substance
lessons.description: Calculate molar mass from a formula and use it to find amount in moles.
lessons.content: Molar mass is the mass of one mole of a substance, expressed in g mol⁻¹. Add the relative atomic masses for every atom shown in the formula. Amount in moles is found from n = m ÷ M.
learning_objectives: Calculate molar mass from a chemical formula.
Find amount in moles from sample mass and molar mass.
prerequisites: Read subscripts in chemical formulae and perform arithmetic.

explanation_sections.title: Adding formula masses
explanation_sections.body: For water, H₂O, use two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom: Mᵣ = (2 × 1) + 16 = 18. The molar mass has the same numerical value in g mol⁻¹.

explanation_sections.title: Mass-to-moles calculation
explanation_sections.body: Use n = m/M, where m is mass in grams and M is molar mass in g mol⁻¹. The units cancel to give moles. Recap: calculate M carefully before dividing the sample mass.

worked_examples.prompt: Find the amount of substance in 9 g of water. Use H=1 and O=16.
worked_examples.reasoning: M(H₂O) = 18 g mol⁻¹, so n = 9 g ÷ 18 g mol⁻¹ = 0.5 mol.

lessons.author: ElimuQuest Curriculum Team

questions.prompt: What is the molar mass of carbon dioxide, CO₂? Use C=12 and O=16.
How many moles are in 10 g of a substance with molar mass 20 g mol⁻¹?
What is the correct unit for molar mass?
questions.explanation: Molar mass expresses grams of substance per mole.

lessons.title: Concentration of solutions
lessons.description: Calculate concentration in mol dm⁻³ using amount and solution volume.
lessons.content: Concentration describes the amount of dissolved substance in a given volume of solution. In molar concentration, c = n/V when volume V is measured in dm³. Convert cm³ to dm³ by dividing by 1000.
learning_objectives: Use c = n/V with consistent volume units.
Convert solution volume between cm³ and dm³.

explanation_sections.title: Concentration relationship
explanation_sections.body: Concentration c is amount n divided by solution volume V. If n is in moles and V in dm³, c is in mol dm⁻³. A larger amount in the same volume gives a higher concentration.

explanation_sections.title: Volume conversion
explanation_sections.body: There are 1000 cm³ in 1 dm³. Convert before substituting: 250 cm³ = 0.250 dm³. Recap: write the volume in dm³ first, then divide moles by volume.

worked_examples.prompt: Find the concentration of 0.10 mol dissolved to make 0.50 dm³ of solution.
